newsitem.title: UK: Engineering stocks dragged down by Vickers.
newsitem.headline: Engineering stocks dragged down by Vickers.

text.p: Shares in British engineering stocks traded lower on Thursday,after a profits warning from Vickers Plc shook up the sector, dealers said.

Vickers shares were down 21 pence, or 9.29 percent, to 205p by 1330 GMT in volume of 2.5 million. TI Group Plc was off 18.5p (3.38 percent) at 529p on turnover of 1.8 million and Siebe Plc lost 18p (1.88 percent) to 937p, with 1.7 million shares traded.
Meanwhile, the FTSE-100 index was little changed on the day, down just 2.1 points, or 0.05 percent, at 4,389.8.
"The (engineering) sector has underperformed over the past month or so and now we've got the currency story," a market-maker at a British bank said.
Vickers chairman Richard Lloyd told shareholders at its annual meeting of "the difficulties which the high relative value of sterling was causing us across our businesses".

"Export orders - and let me remind you that in recent years Vickers has exported on average about 50 percent of our UK turnover - are proving harder to obtain and profit margins on them tend to be thinning," Lloyd said.
